_comment: The pinned inputs, as a set. Everything this project stores -- the corpus vectors, the
recorded query vectors, the recorded model answers and the grades over them -- is a
function of the entries below. Each one records what that input currently hashes to, so
that changing one and forgetting to rebuild what was made with it fails loudly instead of
passing quietly.
No value here is a copy of a value that lives somewhere else. The catalog's own SHA-256 is
in catalog/pinned.json and the model's revision is in embedder.json; what an entry holds is
a digest derived from those at check time. Two records of one number is one record and one
stale copy, and for the catalog the stale copy would be the one people quote, because that
hash is computable by anyone who downloads the file.
`identity` is what a person reads and `digest` is what the check enforces, and they are
compared separately because they fail differently. A moved identity is an announced change
nobody re-recorded. A moved digest under an unchanged identity is the one a version string
cannot catch: somebody changed what a module produces and did not say so.
NOT ALL CHANGES HERE COST THE SAME, and `invalidates` on each entry is the record of that.
A prompt-template change invalidates recorded answers and the grades over them, and leaves
the corpus alone. AN EMBEDDER CHANGE INVALIDATES EVERYTHING -- corpus vectors, recorded
query vectors, every recorded answer and every grade -- because different vectors retrieve
different control ids, and those ids and their text sit inside the prompt every recorded
call is keyed on. There is no partial re-record for an embedder swap. This file detects the
mismatch; it cannot repair it.
`identity` and `digest` are null together when this build does not have that input at all.
The entry still exists, with what it covers and what it costs written down, so that
building it later is a regeneration of a known entry rather than a new mechanism arriving
with its cost undecided.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: the corpus fingerprint. Floating-point results depend on the BLAS
kernels torch selects for the hardware it is on, so two machines can produce vectors equal
to every decimal anyone cares about and differing in the last bit. Pinning that number here
would fail on a second machine for a reason nobody could act on. It is recorded in the
database by the ingest that produced it, where it means what it can mean: on this machine,
with these inputs, re-running changed nothing.
ALSO DELIBERATELY ABSENT: library and interpreter versions. pyproject.toml pins torch and
sentence-transformers exactly and bounds the interpreter, each with a comment saying why.
The lockfile pins the environment; this file pins the inputs.
`make manifest` checks. `make manifest-write` records a change, and never runs on its own --
a check that repaired what it found would be a record of whatever was on disk when it ran.
Its diff belongs in the pull request that explains the change.

catalog.covers: The pinned NIST SP 800-53 release and the vendored file it was pinned to, including the counts a correct copy parses to.

parameter_resolution.covers: How the catalog's parameter markers are rendered into readable slots, over every part at every depth.

chunker.covers: How a live control or enhancement becomes a retrievable chunk: its text, its identifiers, and the order they come in.

embedder.covers: The pinned embedding model, its revision, and every property of it that decides what a vector comes out as.

_comment: Not built. The template that turns retrieved chunks and a question into a request:
its instructions, its layout, and the order the retrieved text appears in. Recorded
answers are keyed on the whole rendered request, so one changed character is a miss
rather than a stale hit -- which is the point, and which is why the cost below is
already written down.
prompt_template.covers: The template that renders retrieved chunks and a question into the request a model is sent.

_comment: Not built. The generation model's own tokenizer, pinned beside the model version.
A generic or approximate one means counting a number the provider does not bill
against, so swapping it changes every counted size without changing a stored artefact:
nothing has to be re-recorded, and every number previously reported is wrong.
tokenizer.covers: The tokenizer prompt sizes are counted with, pinned beside the generation model it belongs to.

_comment: Not built. The prompt an automated grader is given to score an answer against the
controls it cited. Grades are recorded like any other model call, so they are keyed on
this and a change to it invalidates them -- and only them, because grading reads an
answer that already exists rather than producing one.
judge_prompt.covers: The prompt an automated grader is given to score an answer against the controls it cited.
